body.call: Hi, this is {rep} from TechNext. You asked us about Odoo, so I'm calling to confirm a few details before we meet. Is now a good time for two minutes?
body.sms: Hi {name}, this is {rep} from TechNext. I tried to call about your Odoo enquiry. When is a good time for a 5-minute call? You can also reply here.
body.video:
Hi {name}, looking forward to our meeting on {slot}. Here is a 5-minute video about TechNext, so you know who we are before we meet: {video}

If anything changes on your side, just let me know.
body.deckPrompt: Use the technext-sales-proposal skill to build a TechNext presentation (technext-presentations template) for {company_full}, {profile}. Current system: {system}. Main problem in their words: "{words}". Contact: {name}. Return the published link.

a.name: Thank you
a.ask: Anything more you need before the next step?
a.t: {name}, thank you for your time today with Neil and me. You mentioned: "{words}" We will keep that at the centre of our proposal. Is there anything more you need from us before {next}? – {rep}, TechNext

a.name: Point to the section
a.tag: Where the proposal answers their concern
a.t: Hi {name}, I have sent our proposal to your email. Since you raised [the {tool} problem], section [x] explains how we would approach it. Is anything in that section unclear? – {rep}

a.name: Priorities recap
a.ask: Did I get your priorities right?
a.t:
Subject: {company} – your priorities and where the proposal covers them

Dear {name},

Here is a short summary of what you told us, so it is easy to share with your team:
1. "{words}" – section [x]: moving your {area} to Odoo.
2. [{rule} compliance, only if they raised it] – section [y].
3. [Production, if raised] – noted for a later phase, not in Phase 1.

Did I get your priorities right?

Regards,
{rep}

a.name: One useful item
a.ask: Is this useful for your team?
a.t: Hi {name}, a short read you may find useful: [approved item, e.g. how a company moved its records from {tool} to Odoo, link]. It covers [one point from the item]. Would something like this be useful for your team? – {rep}

a.name: One-pager offer
a.ask: Would a version for the decision maker help?

a.name: Keep the file open?
a.ask: Keep it open, or close it for now?
a.t: Hi {name}, I don't want to fill your inbox while your team is busy. Should I keep the {company} file open, or close it for now? Either answer is fine, and you can message me anytime. – {rep}

b.name: Thank you
b.ask: Anything more you need before the next step?
b.t: {name}, thank you for meeting Neil and me today. I hope it was useful for the {company} team. Is there anything more you need from us before {next}? – {rep}, TechNext

b.name: Offer a walk-through
b.ask: [Day A] or [Day B] for a short call?
b.t: Hi {name}, our proposal is now in your email. Would a short call on [Day A] or [Day B] help, so we can go through it together, with {owner} too if useful? – {rep}

b.name: One point + two times
b.t:
Subject: {company} proposal – one point

Dear {name},

One point worth knowing: the proposal keeps Phase 1 to {phase1} and leaves {later} for later, so [the {tool} problem] comes first.

Would [Day A] or [Day B] suit you for a short call?

Regards,
{rep}

b.name: Reply 1, 2 or 3
b.t:
Hi {name}, to save you time, just reply with a number:
1 – Still reviewing the proposal
2 – You need something from us
3 – On hold for now
Any answer helps me plan. – {rep}

b.name: Item + invite the boss
b.t:
Subject: {company} – a short call with {owner}?

Dear {name},

In case it helps the review: [approved item, e.g. a short note on moving data from {tool}, link]. Neil and I can also walk {owner} through the proposal with you.

Would [Day A] or [Day B] work?

Regards,
{rep}

b.name: Closing the loop
b.t:
Subject: Closing the loop on the {company} proposal

Dear {name},

I know your team is busy, so I will pause my follow-ups on the Odoo proposal for now. If the {project} comes back on your list, just reply to this email.

Thank you again for your time.

Regards,
{rep}

c.name: Name the worry
c.ask: What would you need to see before the next step?
c.t: {name}, thank you for today. It seems like [moving the {area} data out of {tool} safely] is what worries your team most. What would you need to see from us before {next}? – {rep}

c.name: Anything off target?
c.t:
Subject: {company} proposal – is anything off target?

Dear {name},

Thank you again for our meeting. The proposal is attached. In short, Phase 1 covers what you raised with {phase1}, and {later} is left for later, as we discussed.

Is anything in it off target for {company}?

Regards,
{rep}

c.name: Against a one-pager?
c.ask: Are you against a one-page summary?
c.t: Hi {name}, you mentioned {owner} will look at this too. Would you be against me preparing a one-page summary you can forward, using only what is already in the proposal? – {rep}

c.name: Soft label, my fault
c.tag: Name the silence, take the blame
c.ask: What would make this easier on your side?
c.t: Hi {name}, it seems like I may not have made something clear in the proposal, or other priorities came up at {company}. Either is understandable. What would make this easier to move forward on your side? – {rep}

c.name: Have you given up?

items.note: Tách từ bản T&S 05/11; chờ Neil duyệt

go: Thank them and confirm the agreed next step. The sequence stops.
Thank you, {name}. Let's go ahead with {next}. Would [Day A] or [Day B] work for you and {owner}? – {rep}
q: Answer only from the proposal or approved content. If unsure, check with Neil first. Then the plan restarts.
Thanks for asking, {name}. [Answer from the proposal or approved content.] If it helps, Neil can join a short call. – {rep}
obj: Treat it as a need for information: one approved item that speaks to it, plus one question. Don't argue by message. A new price goes to the Approver first.
Thank you for telling me, {name}. This may help: [approved item that speaks to the concern, link]. Which part matters most to cover first? – {rep}
int: Of course, {name}. Would a one-page summary for {owner} help? It would use only what is already in the proposal. – {rep}
later: Ask permission to send one useful note a month.
Understood, {name}. Would it be all right if I send one useful note a month until the timing is better? – {rep}
no: Thank them and mark the lead lost.
Thank you for letting me know, {name}. I'll close the file on our side. If anything changes, you can message me anytime. – {rep}

go: Book the call right away. The sequence stops.
Great, thank you {name}. Would [Day A] at [time] or [Day B] at [time] work for a call with Neil? – {rep}
q: Answer briefly, then offer one call slot if a call would help. Then the plan restarts.
Good question, {name}. [Short answer.] If a call is easier, would [Day A] work? – {rep}
obj: Acknowledge it in one line, answer from approved content, offer a call. A price change goes to the Approver first.
Understood, {name}, thank you for being direct. [One-line answer from approved content.] Would a short call on [Day A] or [Day B] help us look at options? – {rep}
int: Ask when to check back and follow that timing. Offer a call with the decision maker.
Of course, {name}. When would be a good time for me to check back? Neil and I can also walk {owner} through it on a short call. – {rep}
later: Ask permission for a light monthly check-in. (B4 reply "3" means this too.)
Understood, {name}. Is it all right if I check in once a month until the timing is better? – {rep}
no: Stop and thank them. Efti stops after a no.
Thank you for letting me know, {name}. I'll pause on our side. If the project comes back, just reply here. – {rep}

go: Name what you hear, ask how they want to proceed, then book the step.
It sounds like the timing is right for {company} now, {name}. How would you like to proceed? – {rep}
q: Answer, then label until you hear "That's right". Then the plan restarts.
[Answer.] It seems like the main concern is [their concern, in their words]. Is that right? – {rep}
obj: Voice the worry they may have, name the obstacle, move to a call. A price change goes to the Approver first.
You may feel this is a big change for {team}, {name}. It seems like [the obstacle] is what is holding this back. Would you be against a short call with Neil to look at it? – {rep}
int: Ask how decisions get made at {company} (NEPQ), then offer the one-pager (C3).
Of course, {name}. How do decisions like this usually get made at {company}? Would you be against a one-page summary for {owner}? – {rep}
later: Let them set the timing, then check back once on that date.
Would it be a bad idea for me to check back after [the period they name], {name}? – {rep}
no: Accept it and part on good terms. In "No, but…", the "but" is the real obstacle: ask about it.
Thank you for telling me, {name}. I appreciate the honesty. If anything changes, I'm here. – {rep}

body.b: B4 answers: "1" still reviewing → ask when to check back. "2" needs something → ask what. "3" on hold → Not now.
body.c: Use "Have you given up…?" only after silence, and only about their own goal, never "our proposal".

greet.a: {name}, thank you for confirming today's meeting, and for the chance to speak with you and the {company} team. I'm {rep} from TechNext. With me is Neil, our solution architect, who leads our Odoo projects.
greet.b: Hi {name}, thank you for having us and for confirming this slot. A quick round of names first: I'm {rep}, I'll guide today's session, and Neil will take the technical questions. May I ask who is joining from your side, and your role?

expect.a: Here is the plan for the next 30 minutes. First a short video about TechNext and Odoo. Then most of the time is yours: we'd like to understand how invoices, books and {rule} filings work at {company} today. At the end we agree on the next step together. Does that work for you?
expect.b: We'll keep this to about 30 minutes, in three parts: a five-minute video, your questions and how you work today, and a clear next step. If something more urgent is on your mind, tell us now and we'll start there.

close.a: Thank you, this was very useful. So I can send you a summary today, may I confirm your email and mobile number? And who else at {company} should receive it?
close.b: Before we end, let's agree the next step. I suggest a 30-minute call next week with your decision maker to go through a draft scope. Would [day] or [day] work?

body.video_before: Let me share a short video, about five minutes, so you can see who we are and what Odoo looks like for {segment}. After that the floor is yours.
body.video_after: That's the overview. What stood out for you, and what did we not cover that matters to {company}?
body.qa_intro: May I ask a few questions, so we understand how {company} works today?

items.note: Tách từ bản T&S 05/11; chờ Neil duyệt

it: What exactly fails in your current system? Which version, and can the data still be exported?
How many people would use the new system?
Which other tools or files does it connect to today?
Who looks after the system now, in-house or an outside provider?
finance: Where are invoices and books being produced right now?
Which tax or e-invoicing rules apply to you, and by when?
Do you report to a parent company, and in which currency?
How long does month-end closing take today?
owner: Is the budget a floor or a ceiling? Does it include licences?
What would a good result look like in six months?
What is the ideal timing to go live?
ops: How do orders or RFQs arrive today, who quotes, and how long does it take?
Which machines or sites does the system need to cover?
Where do jobs get tracked today: paper, spreadsheets or a system?
